question.prompt: In an equilateral triangle each interior angle is trisected by a pair of rays. The intersection of the interiors of the middle \(20^\circ\)-angle at each vertex is the interior of a convex hexagon. What is the degree measure of the smallest angle of this hexagon?

solutions.title: Find the two types of hexagon angles
solutions.explanation:
The trisectors form two useful types of intersections: matching rays that make \(40^\circ\) with a triangle side, and matching rays that make \(20^\circ\) with that side.

Name the equilateral triangle \(ABC\). Each vertex angle is \(60^\circ\). Let \(P\) be the intersection of the rays from \(A\) and \(B\) making \(40^\circ\) with \(AB\) and \(BA\), respectively. Let \(Q\) be the intersection of the corresponding \(20^\circ\) rays. Reflection symmetry puts both points on the angle bisector from \(C\), inside its middle \(20^\circ\) sector. Thus both are vertices of the hexagon.

At \(P\), the common region opens toward \(AB\), so the hexagon's interior angle is \(\angle APB\). The triangle angle sum gives
\[
\angle APB=180^\circ-40^\circ-40^\circ=100^\circ.
\]
At \(Q\), first calculate
\[
\angle AQB=180^\circ-20^\circ-20^\circ=140^\circ.
\]
Here the hexagon opens along the continuations of \(AQ\) and \(BQ\) beyond \(Q\). Its interior angle is vertically opposite \(\angle AQB\), so it also measures \(140^\circ\).

Rotating the configuration by \(120^\circ\) produces three vertices of each type, accounting for all six vertices. The smallest angle is therefore \(\boxed{100^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
